newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Olympia says gets gaming licence.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Olympia says gets gaming licence.

text.p: Malaysian gaming firm Olympia Industries Bhd said on Friday that it had obtained a gaming licence from the Ministry of Finance for its operations in eastern Sabah state.
The licence was received on March 22, Olympia said in a statement.
Olympia said it was making arrangements to submit the necessary applications to the relevant authority in Sabah for the issuance of trading licences.

But Sabah Chief Minister Yong Teck Lee had said in January that the state government would not budge from its decision made last year not to renew business licences of all premises selling lottery tickets that have links with Diriwan Corp Bhd, a wholly-owned unit of Olympia.
Olympia, which is 54.7 percent owned by Mycom Bhd, had its gaming licence revoked by the ministry in January last year. Olympia had appealed against the decision.
Diriwan held the gaming licence for lotteries Corp Sdn Bhd which operated about 200 gaming outlets in Sabah before the licence was revoked.
Olympia reported a 35 percent decline in net earnings for the year ended June 30, 1996 to 44.78 million ringgit, which it said was partially due to the loss of the gaming licence.
Olympia has asked for continued suspension of its stock on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange for a further five market days "so as to avoid unnecessary speculations on the company's shares".
The shares, suspended since March 24, were last traded at 2.84 ringgit.
